authenticate.sense: Proving identity to a volume or server (the technical act behind signing in).

busy.note: The disabled-menu-item marker (busy) and a service or port that can't take more work; a volume someone holds open is in-use.
busy.sense: Occupied and unable to take the request right now (a menu item's (busy) marker, a provider or system too busy to answer).

byte.sense: The size unit, and raw bytes shown by the viewer.

column.sense: A column in the file list, a table, or the viewer (Name column, column width).

cursor.sense: The file-list cursor (the highlighted row keyboard commands act on), or the viewer's text cursor.

debugging.sense: Finding the cause of a problem (logs kept for debugging, a debugging mode).

entry.sense: One record in a scan, an index, or a credential store (a Keychain entry, an indexed image entry).

exclude.sense: Leaving a folder or file out of indexing or search on purpose.

git-branch.sense: A git branch, shown by the virtual git portal and git status.

git-repository.sense: A git repository, or the Cmdr repository on GitHub.

grant.sense: Giving an app a permission (grant full disk access, grant Cmdr access).

history.sense: A record of past actions (the operation history, file history, recent searches).

importance.sense: Cmdr's ranking of how much a folder matters to the user (the importance threshold, important folders).

key-combination.sense: The set of keys that make up a shortcut, while recording or checking it.

load.sense: Reading data into the app or into memory (loading suggestions, loading a model, load more rows).

network.sense: The computer network in general (the network connection, the Network group, network hosts).

original.sense: The source files a copy or move leaves behind or takes from.

placeholder.sense: The example text in an empty field, or a stand-in value the user replaces.

rate-limit.sense: A provider refusing requests because too many came too fast.

register-shortcut.sense: Claiming a system-wide key combination with the OS.

removable.sense: A drive that can be ejected and unplugged (USB stick, SD card).

renew.sense: Extending a subscription license for another period.

reply.sense: The AI's answer in an Ask Cmdr chat, or a logged model response.

request.sense: A call sent to an API, a server, or a tool (an AI request, a permission request).

revoke.sense: Taking back a permission or a key that was granted before.

runtime.sense: The bundled local-AI runtime that has to be installed before a local model can run.

sign-up.sense: Joining the occasional-updates mailing list from onboarding or Settings.

source-available.sense: Cmdr's code being public to read (not open source).

subscription.sense: A license that runs for a period and is renewed.

technical-details.sense: The expandable section under an error that shows the system code.

this-mac.sense: The user's own computer, named as the Mac Cmdr runs on.

untouched.sense: Files Cmdr guarantees it didn't change (the originals after a failed transfer).

valid.sense: Whether a license key, a name, or a value is acceptable.

wildcard.sense: The * and ? characters in a filename pattern.

working-tree.sense: The checked-out files of a git repository, in ordinary prose.

worktree.sense: Git's own name for a linked checkout, kept verbatim by the @key descriptions.
